description: Prospective, independently adjudicated EN/PL whole-question corpus, authored before provider evaluation. All cases are held_out and use supported local concepts or explicit fallback/clarification where facts are absent or criteria are underspecified. Gold plans encode the complete intended proposition; guards call out nearby interpretations that must not be substituted.

cases.question: Is the target more populous than Poland but smaller in area than Germany?
guards: Keep Poland and Germany as named comparison entities, not target identities.
Compare population to population and area to area; retain both clauses.
cases.notes: Two independent comparisons use explicitly named reference-country facts and different target relations.

cases.question: Czy powierzchnia jest co najmniej tak duża jak Portugalii, a populacja mniejsza niż Grecji?
guards: Co najmniej includes equality for area; population remains a strict comparison.
Portugal and Greece are references, not proposed target countries.
cases.notes: Combines an inclusive threshold against Portugal with a strict population comparison against Greece.

cases.question: Does its common name begin with ‘M’, contain exactly two words, and have more than 8 characters?
guards: Use common English display name, not a native or official long name.
All three text predicates are conjunctive.
cases.notes: Combines literal prefix, exact word count, and strict character-count boundary on the documented common-name relation.

cases.question: Is its name either exactly three words or ending in ‘-guay’, while also having no space?
guards: The final no-space condition applies to both OR branches.
The quoted suffix is literal text, not a country-name identity.
cases.notes: Nested disjunction must remain under the conjunction with a separate negated space predicate.

cases.question: Is Warsaw its capital, or does it border Czechia while having an area no greater than Austria?
guards: Warsaw is a capital-value literal, not a country entity.
Czechia and Austria occur only in the second OR branch; keep its border and area clauses conjoined.
cases.notes: One branch checks capital identity; the other requires both a named border and inclusive area comparison.

cases.question: Does it border a country that belongs to the EU but is not in NATO?
guards: Both membership predicates bind the same bordering-country item.
Do not test the target's own EU/NATO memberships.
cases.notes: The existential country-valued border list is filtered by EU membership and lack of NATO membership on that same item.

cases.question: Czy każde państwo graniczące z celem ma niemiecki jako język urzędowy?
guards: German official status is checked for every bordering-country item, not for the target.
This tests legal official-language listing, not how widely German is spoken.
cases.notes: A universal scoped predicate over country-valued neighbors; no claim about language prevalence.

cases.question: Are none of its land neighbors islands?
guards: Negation scopes over existence of any island neighbor; do not negate only the item property outside the quantifier.
The item is a bordering country, not a water body.
cases.notes: ‘None’ is not(any matching neighbor); the bound item has the scalar country island property.

cases.question: Does at least one neighbor have either the euro or the Swiss franc listed as a currency?
guards: Both alternative currency tests apply to the same bordering country.
Use currency-list membership; do not count currencies or treat the target as the item.
cases.notes: A country-valued neighbor quantifier contains an OR of two supported currency-list predicates.

cases.question: Does every country it borders lie in Europe or have a population above 20 million?
guards: The OR is evaluated separately for each bordering country under ALL.
The numeric threshold is strict and applies to each item, not the target.
cases.notes: Tests binding/scope where each neighbor may satisfy either continental membership or its own strict population threshold.

cases.question: Czy leży w Afryce i graniczy z krajem o populacji wynoszącej co najmniej 30 milionów?
guards: Africa is physical continent membership of the target.
At least 30 million includes equality and is evaluated on a border-country item.
cases.notes: Conjoins a target continent-list condition with an existential country-valued neighbor population test.

cases.question: Is it in Oceania but not in the Southern Hemisphere?
guards: The question negates Southern-hemisphere membership only; it does not assert Northern membership.
Oceania uses the physical continent relation, not a guessed regional substitute.
cases.notes: Combines broad physical continent membership and explicit territory hemisphere negation without adding an unstated northern condition.

cases.question: Does it have recorded access to the Indian Ocean and an area below 1,200,000 km²?
guards: Indian Ocean is a named ocean-access condition, not a generic coast test.
The area bound is strict; both conditions are conjunctive.
cases.notes: Combines an explicit recorded ocean-access list value with an independent area threshold.

cases.question: Does it have a land border and a population below 750,000?
guards: A land border means nonempty known country border list, not water access.
Population threshold is strict.
cases.notes: Pairs existence of at least one recorded land-bordering country with an independent strict population bound.

cases.question: Does it border France or have Portuguese as an official language, but not both?
guards: ‘But not both’ is exclusive-or: preserve both exclusive branches.
Official-language listing does not mean Portuguese is widely spoken.
cases.notes: Explicit truth conditions are (France border AND no Portuguese official language) OR (no France border AND Portuguese official language).

cases.question: Is Christianity the dominant religion and is the country outside the EU?
guards: Christianity includes Catholic OR Orthodox OR Protestant OR generic Christianity in the stored dominant category.
Do not infer Christianity from language or culture; EU negation is a separate conjunct.
cases.notes: Faith categories are alternatives under an AND with not(EU membership); neither cultural proxies nor target language are relevant.

cases.question: Czy dominującą kategorią religijną jest islam, a rząd ma formę monarchii?
guards: Islam is the exact grouped dominant-religion value, not a general prevalence estimate.
Monarchy is the broad stored form; no constitutional/absolute subtype is implied.
cases.notes: Conjoins two exact supported scalar categories in Polish wording.

cases.question: Does its constitution establish Catholicism as the state religion?
guards: Do not substitute the dominant-religion category for constitutional establishment.
Do not infer legal state religion from majority belief.
cases.notes: Objective constitutional state-religion status is not represented by dominant_religion and requires external legal facts.

cases.question: Are more than 60 percent of its residents Muslim?
guards: Do not treat a dominant-religion label as a numeric population share.
The precise percentage asks prevalence data, not category equality.
cases.notes: The numerical resident share is absent even though broad dominant-religion categories are supported.

cases.question: Is its latitude north of Italy's and its longitude west of Greece's?
guards: North means greater signed latitude; west means smaller signed longitude.
Italy and Greece are reference countries, and point coordinates do not assert territorial extent.
cases.notes: Combines two independent signed-coordinate comparisons to different named references.

cases.question: Does its territory include both Eastern and Western Hemispheres, and is it in Asia?
guards: Both hemisphere memberships describe territory and are conjunctive; do not substitute point longitude.
Asia is physical continent membership, not a regional-area guess.
cases.notes: Tests two-sided territory hemisphere membership alongside an independent physical-continent condition.

cases.question: Does the recorded major-river list include the Danube while the country has an area above 400,000 km²?
guards: River-list membership is a recorded major-river fact, not a claim that the river only occurs there.
Area is strictly greater than 400,000 km².
cases.notes: Conjoins a direct major-river list query with a numeric area lower bound.

cases.question: Does its flag include both blue and a crescent symbol?
guards: Blue is a color-presence test; crescent is a symbol-presence test.
Both presences are required; no proportion, layout, or exclusivity is asserted.
cases.notes: Combines two distinct supported flag relations without inferring area or arrangement.

cases.question: Does red cover at least one third of its flag?
guards: Do not replace a proportional-area claim with flag_color contains red.
The fraction is an objective but unrepresented flag measurement.
cases.notes: Flag colors are represented only as presence, not share of area.

cases.question: Was it part of the Austro-Hungarian Empire historically, and is it currently in NATO?
guards: Past polity membership and current NATO membership are separate relations and time frames.
Do not infer one predicate from the other.
cases.notes: Pairs one listed past polity with present organization membership while preserving temporal distinction.

cases.question: Was it ever a member of NATO before 1990?
guards: Current membership cannot answer an ‘ever before 1990’ historical-membership question.
Do not infer past status from present membership or vice versa.
cases.notes: Past membership in an active organization and a date-bounded historical period are not represented.

cases.question: Is it currently in the EU but absent from the historical Warsaw Pact list?
guards: EU is current membership; Warsaw Pact absence is checked only in historical_union.
Do not treat Warsaw Pact and Eastern Bloc as synonyms.
cases.notes: Combines a present-state positive list test with a historical-polity negative list test.

cases.question: Does it lie in Europe or Asia, but not in South America?
guards: The exclusion applies after the Europe-or-Asia disjunction; preserve its outer AND with NOT South America.
Use physical continent membership, not geographic-area tags or a claim of entire territorial extent.
cases.notes: The complete condition is (Europe OR Asia) AND NOT South America, retaining all three continent clauses.

cases.question: Is it in the Caribbean and classified as a republic?
guards: Caribbean is the stored geographic-area tag, not a cultural or language label.
Republic is the broad stored government type and does not imply democracy.
cases.notes: Pairs an explicit regional tag with an exact supported government-form category.

cases.question: Is its national culture predominantly Slavic?
guards: Do not substitute geographic_area, official_language, or a neighboring-country fact for culture.
The cultural category has no local relation.
cases.notes: This asks an objective-sounding but culturally defined classification absent from the supported country facts.

cases.question: Does the official long-form country name contain the letter ‘e’?
guards: The name relation is the common English display name, not the official long-form name.
Do not apply a supported common-name substring test to an unsupported name variant.
cases.notes: Official-name text is absent; its letter property cannot be answered using the common display name.

cases.question: Is it relatively small compared with nearby countries?
guards: No comparison set or measurable definition of ‘small’ is specified.
Do not invent nearby countries from borders or assume area/population as the intended size measure.
cases.notes: The request lacks both an objective meaning for ‘small’ and a defined reference group, so neither a local predicate nor factual fallback can be chosen.
